title: Prove linear Gaussian-dyadic tensor widths for the full n-qubit Clifford alphabet
body:
For raw tensor columns from one Gaussian-dyadic unitary per projective n-qubit Clifford class, this gives an exact left inverse at every width f ≥ 3n+2 for odd n ≥ 3 and f ≥ 3n+1 for even n ≥ 4. Five and six qubits therefore need at most **17 and 19** copies. Compared with the code-based construction explained in the note, this lowers the five- and six-qubit sufficient widths from 25 to 17 and 19. At five qubits the known lower bound is 13. Sharpness beyond four qubits remains open.

The Bell correction works for both tuple parities. At odd pair count, the linear observation recovers a weighted sum of conjugated operators while preserving the original complex mixture coefficients. A dyadic group-algebra identity then separates the symplectic fibres. The proof gives the normalization rule for odd n and distinguishes the coefficient ring for raw and normalized data.

The replay covers 33,866 characters through five qubits, higher-dimensional rank representatives, 32,640 scalar-lift/tuple cases, 12,240 cocycle checks, and direct five- and six-qubit mixture blocks. Credit goes to Ali Romman, Nick Petalas, MatShep and alephnan for the spectral and width results, and to the preceding dyadic constructions in #7797–#7799. The package establishes an algebraic width bound. The runtime and noise budget for a full implementation remain open.
